title: a manifest with an ordinary kernel pattern that also carries a `blocks[]` section must fail loudly, in both languages
why: This is row25's fixture with one change: the top-level `pattern` is an
ordinary, launch-certified kernel pattern instead of `neural_block`, so
both dispatch gates pass it through and reach the check under test rather
than rejecting on an unrecognized or wrong-family pattern. It is normal
for two fixtures with different content to share the same row number,
since they check the same rule at two related points.
Before this check existed, a kernel-pattern manifest carrying a `blocks[]`
section was silently ignored in both languages and its entries loaded as
bare kernels — exactly the kind of misread this fixture exists to catch.
Before the fix, this exact fixture could not pass by accident: Python
used to fail reaching for a nonexistent kernel artifact with a file-not-found
error rather than a validation error, and C++ failed on the same missing
artifact with an unrelated message, so this fixture could only pass once
the check was added and made to fire before any artifact is loaded.
Both languages now reject with the same shared message text saying that a
manifest carrying `blocks[]` must declare the `neural_block` pattern; each
language appends its own additional detail after that shared text.
